main_text.p: armamentarium, & machinas varii generis ad expeditiones maritimas & oppugnationes urbium paratas, quarum struendarum ipsa erat studiosa ac perita: & quia agrum possidebat non admodum felicem, oleas quidem & vites ferentem, sed frumento sterilem, maritimæ magis rei quàm agriculturæ dabat operam. Atque his studiis & apparatu, Romanis sociis & adjutoribus suis,magno sæpe usui vicissim fuit. Spoliis ex hoste frequenter potita, ea velut virtutis suæ & victoriarum monumenta locis publicis suffigere, atque ad posteros transmittere in more habebat. In operibus ejus publicis cum alia erant, tum templa spectatu digna, quorum duo in urbis parte editiore, quam arcem vocabant, alterum Dianæ Ephesinæ, alterum Apollini Delphico sacrum, quòd horum ꝯuminum auspiciis primi conditores urbem hîc struxisse ferebatur, præcipuâ religione colebantur. Coloniæ ejus feruntur, Rhoë Agatha ad orientem versus ostia Rhodani, Taurentium, Olbia, Antipolis, Niciæa atque occidentem, versus Italiam, omnes litori vicinæ. page.notes: The Greek word after "concilium" is uncertain in its first letters: transcribed as (συνέδριον with [?] in mind; the scan is faint there. The right and left edges show parts of the neighbouring page and are excluded. The word "ferebatur" is printed as "ferebat" and "tur" across a line end; the printed hyphen is not clearly visible, so it is written whole. Line-end hyphens are kept where printed: ar-cem, ad-modum, da-bat, Spo-liis, Mafsilien-ses are as they appear.
